A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same AltLoRA work, with matching core equations and empirical material. V1 cites appendices but ends after its references; v2 supplies Appendices A–E, whose contents can be assessed as newly documented material.

before.justification: V1 reports original fine-tuning results, memory and training-time measurements, and ablations in Tables 2–8 and Figures 1–2.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments in the main text and Appendix E, including benchmark results, efficiency measurements and ablations.

M1.justification: The alternating projection and momentum-update procedure remains unchanged. AltLoRA+ was already described and evaluated in v1; its explicit Algorithm 2 and the regularized projection formulas in v2 supply missing documentation without establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: Both use WizardLM/MT-Bench for dialogue, MetaMathQA/GSM8K for mathematics, CodeFeedBack/HumanEval for code, and the same five GLUE tasks. Appendix E relocates existing evaluations without adding dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches in the LLM, GLUE and efficiency comparisons, including the existing LoRA-Pro and LoRA-Rite comparisons where applicable. The relocated updating-strategy, expert-count and initialization studies also retain their comparator sets.

E3.justification: Previously stated models, ranks, scaling factors, target layers, optimizer defaults, schedules, batch sizes and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. Appendix E.1 newly discloses sample counts, learning-rate grids and the 3000-step limit for existing experiments; it does not establish a protocol revision.

E4.justification: Learning-rate/scaling-factor sensitivity, rank comparisons, alternating versus joint updates, expert counts and initialization were already studied in v1. V2 moves several studies into Appendix E.3 without adding or changing their analyses.

E5.justification: Both specify three runs with different random seeds and mean/standard-deviation reporting for the generation and GLUE experiments. V2 repeats three-seed averaging in Appendix E.1 without introducing a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Reported table values and both heatmaps are unchanged. V1 Tables 5, 6, 7 and 8 correspond to v2 Tables 6, 7, 8 and 5. For example, rank-8 AltLoRA+ still scores 76.91±0.31 on GSM8K with Llama-3.1-8B.

T1.justification: Appendices B and D supply mathematical material absent from v1: projection derivations, regularized corollaries, a formal stable-feature-learning definition and analysis, the momentum-invariance argument, and explicit RIP/cross-correlation assumptions and convergence bounds. These substantially expand the formal support for previously stated claims.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about memory-efficient gradient/momentum projection, stable feature learning, AltLoRA's transformation invariance, convergence and empirical advantages. Additional appendix material supports existing claims without changing their main scope.

C2.justification: Appendix D.2 adds an explanation of why combining aligned second moments with first moments can break invariance and suggests unscaled gradients/momentum as a possible remedy. It also adds an argument about neglected joint-update cross terms in LoRA-Rite. AltLoRA+'s lack of transformation invariance was already acknowledged in v1.

D1.justification: V2 supplies explicit AltLoRA+ pseudocode, instructions for alternating gradient computation in Transformers, and the regularization value λ=10^-6. Appendix E.1 discloses training subsets of 52k/100k/100k examples, method-specific learning-rate grids and the 3000-step limit. These substantially improve documentation of existing methods and experiments; the code-access statement remains unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds four mathematical references supporting pseudoinverses, matrix factorization, convex neural-network formulations and RIP, and replaces the original Llama citation with Llama 2. Appendix D.2 adds positioning against LoRA-Rite's invariance analysis. The existing related-work discussion is otherwise principally relocated.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: Related Work moves from Section 2 to Appendix A, and detailed ablations and additional Llama-3 results move into Appendix E. The main ablation narrative is shortened, sections and cross-references are revised, and technical material is organized into new appendices. Most retained prose changes little.

P2.justification: V2 adopts NeurIPS formatting with a redesigned title/author block, different typography, margins and algorithm styling. Several tables and Figure 2 move into the appendix, and Algorithm 2 gains an explicit display. The existing figures and table contents remain unchanged despite the extensive layout revision.

improvement.justification: V2 remedies important reproducibility omissions: v1 references unavailable appendices and lacks explicit AltLoRA+ pseudocode and key training/search details, which v2 supplies. The theoretical appendices also make assumptions and arguments inspectable. These are substantial gains despite unchanged empirical results. The added convergence proof still contains an unjustified inequality transition from Eq. 57 to Eq. 58, limiting the improvement in theoretical substantiation.
